Buying guide

Buying your first home in Toronto: every cost, step by step

What you need in the bank, what you'll pay at closing, and the six steps from pre-approval to keys, using a real example.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
4-minute readToronto & York RegionUpdated November 2026
The short version
  • On an $800,000 home you need at least $55,000 down, plus roughly $22,000 in closing costs if it's in the City of Toronto.
  • First-time buyers get up to $8,475 back on land transfer tax in Toronto, or up to $4,000 in York Region.
  • You qualify at your rate plus 2% (or 5.25%, whichever is higher), so get pre-approved before you shop.

02Cash you need for an $800,000 home in North York

Example: a first-time buyer with the minimum down payment, buying in the City of Toronto.

03Six steps from savings to keys

  1. 01

    Get your money organized

    Month 1

    Open an FHSA if you haven't, check your credit report, and gather pay stubs and two years of tax notices. Couples can each use an FHSA and the Home Buyers' Plan.

  2. 02

    Get pre-approved

    Month 1–2

    A lender checks you can carry the payment at the qualifying rate. Ask for the rate to be held while you shop.

  3. 03

    Shop and compare

    Month 2–4

    Compare total cost, not just price: land transfer tax, condo fees and commute. Use the land transfer tax calculator on each address.

  4. 04

    Make an offer

    Offer day

    Most buyers include conditions on financing and inspection, and a status certificate review for condos. The deposit is usually due within 24 hours of acceptance.

  5. 05

    Firm up

    About 5 business days

    Clear your conditions: inspection, final mortgage approval, lawyer's review of the status certificate.

  6. 06

    Close

    30–90 days later

    Your lawyer registers the purchase, pays the land transfer tax and claims your rebates. You send the balance a few days before closing and get the keys.

04Where the down payment can come from

FHSA

Up to $40,000

Contributions are tax-deductible; qualifying withdrawals are tax-free.

RRSP: Home Buyers' Plan

Up to $60,000

Withdrawals made 2026–2028 start repaying in the fifth year after, over 15 years.

Both together

Allowed

You can use the FHSA and the Home Buyers' Plan for the same home if you meet both sets of rules.

Gift from family

Common

Lenders usually want a signed gift letter and proof the funds are in your account.

Ali's take

Budget for the closing costs first, then the down payment. The $20,000 or so due at closing is the number first-time buyers most often leave out.

Quick answers

How much do I need for a down payment on an $800,000 home in Toronto?

At least $55,000: 5% of the first $500,000 ($25,000) plus 10% of the remaining $300,000 ($30,000). With less than 20% down, you also pay CMHC mortgage insurance.

Do first-time buyers pay land transfer tax in Toronto?

Yes, but they can get rebates: up to $4,000 on the Ontario tax and up to $4,475 on Toronto's municipal tax, if they meet the eligibility rules. Your lawyer claims them at closing.

Can I use both an FHSA and the Home Buyers' Plan?

Yes. CRA allows a qualifying FHSA withdrawal and a Home Buyers' Plan withdrawal for the same home if you meet the conditions of both.
